diagnosis: Diffuse large B-cell lymphoma, not otherwise specified (DLBCL, NOS), germinal-center B-cell-like (GCB) subtype by the Hans algorithm, involving the right cervical lymph nodes at levels II and III. The diagnosis is established by excisional biopsy of a right level III node (2026-09-04) with diffuse sheets of large atypical B cells, CD20/PAX5 positive, CD10 diffuse positive, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 negative, CD5 and cyclin D1 negative, CD30 negative, EBER negative, and a kappa-restricted CD19/CD20/CD10-positive large B-cell population by flow cytometry. BCL2 is positive in approximately 30% and MYC in approximately 15% of tumor cells, with Ki-67 approximately 55%. Interphase FISH shows no MYC, BCL2, or BCL6 rearrangement. There is no residual follicular or other low-grade component to suggest transformation.
stage: Stage IA (Ann Arbor), limited-stage, non-bulky. FDG PET-CT (2026-09-03) shows a cluster of FDG-avid right cervical nodes at levels II and III, contiguous within a single nodal region; the largest right level IIA node is 3.1 x 2.4 cm (SUVmax 14.2) and the level III node is 2.1 x 1.6 cm (SUVmax 11.8). There is no FDG-avid disease elsewhere: no left cervical, supraclavicular, mediastinal, hilar, axillary, retroperitoneal, mesenteric, pelvic, or inguinal nodes; no splenic, hepatic, osseous, or marrow involvement; no extranodal disease. She has no B symptoms (no fever, drenching night sweats, or weight loss). The age-adjusted IPI is 0 (age <60, stage I, LDH 190 U/L [normal 135-225], ECOG 0, no extranodal sites). The CNS-IPI is also 0. Bone marrow biopsy is not required because PET shows no marrow uptake. The radiology report explicitly describes levels II-III as a single contiguous cervical nodal region; even if one counted them as two cervical regions (stage II), this would remain limited-stage, non-bulky disease and the treatment plan would be unchanged.
biology: This is a GCB DLBCL by immunohistochemistry (CD10 diffuse positive, BCL6 positive, MUM1/IRF4 negative), with a CD5-negative, cyclin D1-negative, CD30-negative, EBER-negative phenotype. BCL2 is positive in about 30% and MYC in about 15% of cells, which is below the usual thresholds for double-expressor DLBCL (BCL2 >=40% and MYC >=40%). FISH is negative for MYC, BCL2, and BCL6 rearrangements, so this is not double-hit or triple-hit lymphoma. Ki-67 is approximately 55%, and there is no necrosis or low-grade component. Overall this is favorable, chemotherapy-sensitive GCB biology without high-risk cytogenetic features. The main biologic uncertainty is that only IHC-based cell-of-origin assignment was performed; gene-expression profiling or NGS/TP53 was not done, but neither is required to select standard first-line R-CHOP.
prognosis: Excellent. With stage IA, aaIPI 0, CNS-IPI 0, GCB biology, no double-hit features, and full fitness, cure is the expected outcome. In the FLYER trial of young patients with favorable limited-stage DLBCL (age <=60, stage I-II, non-bulky, aaIPI 0), four cycles of R-CHOP without radiation produced approximately 96% 3-year progression-free survival and approximately 99% 3-year overall survival. I would quote a greater-than-90% chance of cure and a low relapse risk. The main things that would change this assessment are a positive end-of-treatment PET, a positive pregnancy test (which would force a delay and a pregnancy-specific plan), or a reference pathology review showing high-grade/double-hit biology (very unlikely given the negative FISH). If the end-of-treatment PET is positive, the prognosis is inferior and salvage therapy would be required.
first_line_treatment: Curative-intent R-CHOP21 for four cycles, without involved-site radiation. Regimen: rituximab 375 mg/m2 IV day 1; cyclophosphamide 750 mg/m2 IV day 1; doxorubicin 50 mg/m2 IV day 1; vincristine 1.4 mg/m2 IV (cap 2 mg) day 1; prednisone 100 mg PO daily days 1-5; repeat every 21 days for 4 cycles. This is NCCN-concordant for favorable limited-stage DLBCL and is supported by the FLYER trial (4 cycles of R-CHOP alone was non-inferior to 6 cycles in patients age <=60 with stage I-II, non-bulky, aaIPI 0 disease). I am deliberately omitting ISRT because she has non-bulky stage I disease and strongly wishes to avoid neck radiation given her sister's radiation-related hypothyroidism and her concerns about dry mouth and taste; the tradeoff is one additional cycle of chemotherapy compared with 3 cycles of R-CHOP plus ISRT. I would not use 6 cycles of R-CHOP, Pola-R-CHP, or chemotherapy alone with fewer than 4 cycles. If the end-of-treatment PET shows residual localized disease, I would then use involved-site radiation or salvage platinum-based chemotherapy. If a reference review unexpectedly showed double-hit lymphoma, I would use a more intensive regimen such as DA-EPOCH-R rather than R-CHOP.
cns_risk: Low risk; no CNS prophylaxis indicated. Her CNS-IPI is 0 (age <=60, ECOG 0, normal LDH, no more than one extranodal site, and no kidney/adrenal involvement), which corresponds to a very low risk of CNS relapse (on the order of 1-2% or less). She has no high-risk features such as testicular, breast, adrenal, or bone marrow involvement, double-hit/triple-hit histology, or HIV. I would not give intrathecal methotrexate or high-dose methotrexate prophylaxis. Her migraine with aura is long-standing and typical, with no new neurologic symptoms, so I would not perform a lumbar puncture or brain MRI at baseline. If she develops a new persistent headache, cranial neuropathy, seizures, or other focal neurologic findings, I would reassess with MRI and CSF analysis.
response_assessment: End-of-treatment FDG PET-CT, ideally 6-8 weeks after cycle 4 and not sooner than about 3 weeks after the last chemotherapy, interpreted by Lugano 2014 criteria using the Deauville 5-point scale. I would not do an interim PET outside a clinical trial. Deauville 1-3 constitutes a complete metabolic response. Deauville 4-5 indicates residual disease; in that case I would biopsy the residual node if feasible and either use involved-site radiation for localized residual disease or platinum-based salvage chemotherapy (for example R-ICE or R-DHAP) followed by autologous stem cell transplant if chemosensitive, with CAR-T therapy if refractory. The residual 3 cm right level II node at baseline may persist as fibrosis, so PET rather than size alone determines response. After a complete metabolic response, I would not use routine surveillance PET/CT. Follow-up would be history and examination with blood counts/LDH every 3-6 months for 2 years, then every 6-12 months up to 5 years, with imaging only for symptoms or suspected relapse.
pretreatment_workup: Already complete and adequate: history and examination with ECOG 0; CBC with differential (Hb 13.2 g/dL, WBC 5.9 x10^3/uL, ANC 3.6 x10^3/uL, ALC 1.7 x10^3/uL, platelets 240 x10^3/uL); comprehensive metabolic panel with normal renal and hepatic function (creatinine 0.7 mg/dL, eGFR 108 mL/min/1.73 m2, uric acid 4.6 mg/dL); LDH 190 U/L (normal), beta-2 microglobulin 1.6 mg/L; hepatitis B panel (HBsAg negative, anti-HBc negative, anti-HBs reactive, consistent with vaccine immunity), HCV antibody negative, HIV antigen/antibody negative; staging FDG PET-CT; excisional right cervical lymph node biopsy with immunohistochemistry, flow cytometry, and FISH; and baseline transthoracic echocardiogram with LVEF 63% and normal strain. Bone marrow biopsy is intentionally omitted because PET shows no marrow uptake. Before cycle 1, I still need a serum pregnancy test (she is premenopausal on a combined oral contraceptive), an urgent fertility-preservation consultation (oocyte/embryo cryopreservation, AMH and antral follicle count) because cyclophosphamide is gonadotoxic, a contraception plan, a vaccination review (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal; live vaccines must be avoided during and after rituximab), and consideration of baseline TSH/free T4 given her family history of hypothyroidism and her thyroid concerns. No HBV DNA or antiviral prophylaxis is needed because she is HBsAg/anti-HBc negative and anti-HBs positive. A dental evaluation before anthracycline/steroid therapy is optional but reasonable. No lumbar puncture or brain MRI is needed absent neurologic symptoms.
supportive_care: Stop the combined ethinyl estradiol/levonorgestrel oral contraceptive now. Migraine with aura is a WHO category 4 contraindication to combined hormonal contraception, and active cancer plus chemotherapy further increases venous thromboembolism risk. Switch to a progestin-only or non-hormonal contraceptive method and document a negative pregnancy test before R-CHOP. Continue sumatriptan for migraines as needed; avoid codeine because of the documented allergy. Use guideline-based antiemetics (a 5-HT3 antagonist plus dexamethasone plus an NK1 antagonist, with olanzapine for breakthrough), pegfilgrastim 6 mg subcutaneously 24 hours after each cycle to maintain dose intensity and reduce febrile neutropenia, and constipation prophylaxis with docusate/senna because of vincristine and antiemetics. Tumor lysis risk is low (normal LDH, low bulk, normal renal function): encourage oral hydration and check chemistry 24-48 hours after cycle 1; no rasburicase or allopurinol prophylaxis is needed. No PJP prophylaxis is needed with four cycles of R-CHOP and only five days of prednisone per cycle. No routine VTE anticoagulation is indicated, but maintain mobility, stop the estrogen-containing contraceptive, and have a low threshold for duplex ultrasound if leg swelling occurs; if hospitalized, use pharmacologic prophylaxis. Premedicate rituximab with acetaminophen and diphenhydramine. Cumulative doxorubicin will be 200 mg/m2, and baseline LVEF is normal; repeat echocardiography only for cardiac symptoms. Give inactivated vaccines before or around therapy; live vaccines are contraindicated during and after rituximab until immune reconstitution. Provide fertility counseling, psychosocial/social-work support, and work accommodations around treatment days.
fitness_and_goals: She is fully fit for full-dose, curative-intent therapy: age 45, ECOG 0, normal organ function, LVEF 63%, no cardiac or other major comorbidity, and she works full time as a third-grade teacher. I would not attenuate the R-CHOP doses. Her goals are cure, avoiding neck radiation, and continuing to teach with as few absences as possible; four cycles of R-CHOP alone matches those goals, with treatment every 21 days and schedule adjustments around treatment days. She is undecided about another pregnancy, so fertility preservation should be arranged urgently before cyclophosphamide exposure. A 1-2 week delay for oocyte/embryo retrieval is acceptable in this favorable, non-bulky presentation, but further delay should be avoided. I would involve reproductive endocrinology, social work, and the school early. The main shared decision is four cycles of R-CHOP alone versus three cycles of R-CHOP plus involved-site radiation; I recommend four cycles alone because of her strong radiation-avoidance preference and the FLYER data, accepting one additional cycle of chemotherapy. If she were to become pregnant, R-CHOP would be contraindicated and the plan would change; pregnancy testing and effective contraception are mandatory.
missing_information: Serum pregnancy test before cycle 1; she is premenopausal on a combined oral contraceptive and must be documented non-pregnant before teratogenic chemotherapy.
Fertility-preservation consultation and her decision (oocyte/embryo cryopreservation, AMH/antral follicle count) before cyclophosphamide exposure.
Vaccination status and plan (influenza, COVID-19, pneumococcal; live vaccines must be avoided during and after rituximab).
Baseline TSH/free T4 (optional but reasonable given her family history of hypothyroidism and her thyroid concerns, although no radiation is planned).
An explicit contraception plan after discontinuing the combined oral contraceptive (progestin-only or non-hormonal method).
Confirmation that LDH 190 U/L is within the local reference range; the provided reference range is 135-225 U/L, so it is normal, but this should be documented for IPI/CNS-IPI calculation.
Whether she has any new or atypical neurologic symptoms; currently she has only her usual migraine with aura, so no MRI or lumbar puncture is indicated.
Whether a dental evaluation has been done before anthracycline/steroid therapy (optional, not required to start treatment).

No bone marrow biopsy or CSF analysis was performed; both are intentionally omitted because PET shows no marrow uptake and CNS-IPI is 0. I would obtain a bone marrow biopsy only if PET marrow uptake were equivocal, and CSF only if neurologic symptoms or high-risk features developed.

No NGS/TP53 or gene-expression profiling was performed; neither is required for standard first-line R-CHOP, but gene-expression profiling would refine cell-of-origin assignment if a clinical trial or targeted approach were being considered.
